Franklin Delano Roosevelt. The thirty-second president of the United States, serving from nineteen thirty-three until his death in nineteen forty-five, FDR led the nation for the longest tenure in American history. A distant cousin of Theodore Roosevelt, he led the nation through two monumental crises: the Great Depression and World War Two. His expansive vision of federal power, embodied in the New Deal, reshaped the role of government in American life. Despite being partially paralyzed by polio, he became a symbol of resilience and transformed presidential leadership into a platform for moral persuasion and national unity.

Roosevelt was born in eighteen eighty-two to a wealthy Hudson Valley family. He was educated at Harvard and Columbia Law School and served as a New York state senator before his nineteen ten election. He contracted polio in nineteen twenty-one at age thirty-nine, leaving him paralyzed from the waist down. He kept his disability largely hidden from the public and continued his political career with determination. He served as Assistant Secretary of the Navy under President Woodrow Wilson from nineteen thirteen to nineteen twenty, where he helped oversee naval operations during World War One. He was elected governor of New York in nineteen twenty-eight and ran a moderate reform administration, gaining national prominence by responding to the Depression.

Roosevelt took office during the banking crisis of March nineteen thirty-three. He declared a bank holiday and rallied Americans with his famous first inaugural address: "the only thing we have to fear is fear itself." He enacted the New Deal, a comprehensive program of federal relief, recovery, and reform including the Works Progress Administration, Social Security, the Civilian Conservation Corps, and the National Labor Relations Board. He shifted American political philosophy by arguing the federal government had a responsibility to ensure the welfare of its citizens, dramatically expanding executive and legislative power. He faced fierce opposition from conservatives and the Supreme Court, which declared several early New Deal laws unconstitutional. He responded with the court-packing plan of nineteen thirty-seven, which failed but was a watershed moment in constitutional power.

Roosevelt navigated American isolationism while supporting Britain and China against Nazi Germany and Imperial Japan through Lend-Lease in nineteen forty-one and other aid programs. He met with British Prime Minister Winston Churchill twice at the Atlantic Conference in nineteen forty-one and in Casablanca in nineteen forty-three to coordinate war strategy and establish the Atlantic Charter. He brought America into World War Two after the attack on Pearl Harbor on December seventh, nineteen forty-one. He directed the unconditional surrender doctrine and the strategic bombing campaign against Axis powers. He coordinated with Soviet Premier Joseph Stalin at the Yalta Conference in February nineteen forty-five, where decisions were made about the postwar division of Europe and the creation of the United Nations. Roosevelt died in office on April twelfth, nineteen forty-five, just weeks before Germany's surrender and the end of the war in Europe. Vice President Harry Truman assumed the presidency.
